native_result.query: What kind of demographic disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated?
native_result.HypoA: Gender disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated, with males having higher median wealth than females.
native_result.HypoB: Among ever-incarcerated individuals, 1985 median wealth is very low overall (~$720, ~1/5 of the ~$3,600 non-incarcerated median) with systematic demographic disparities: a racial ordering White (~$2,200) > Black (~$320) > Hispanic (~$0) driven mostly by a higher zero-wealth incidence among Black/Hispanic (39-42% vs 21% for White males), and a sex gap male ($1,000) > female ($0; CI $260-$1,400) that is the most statistically reliable contrast.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspected data (12,013 obs, 6 cols, no missing). 2) Defined ever incarcerated via ever_jailed==1. 3) Computed median composite_wealth_1985 among ever-jailed by race, sex, and race x sex with 4,000-resample bootstrap 95% CIs; reported n per cell. 4) Estimated pairwise median differences with bootstrap CIs; added Mann-Whitney U tests and chi-square tests of zero-wealth incidence. 5) Sensitivity: repeated medians excluding zero-wealth records. 6) Wrote a natural-language hypothesis focusing on within-incarcerated demographic disparities, flagged small female cells (n=9-16) and kept interpretation descriptive (wealth 1985 vs 1985-1994 incarceration window).
